02 | Business Model
Core franchises: institutional active equity, fixed income, private markets. The company combines recurring client relationships
with data-rich workflows that create opportunities for automation, analytics, and differentiated service.
03 | Strategic Priorities
• Modernize data foundations and make financial information easier to discover, validate, and reuse.
• Expand responsible AI in research, service, risk, and workflow automation with strong governance.
• Grow priority client segments while improving operating leverage.
• Maintain conservative capital and liquidity practices appropriate to the business model.

06 | Technology and AI
The company is building a governed AI capability around trusted data, retrieval, workflow automation, and human oversight.
Current use cases include document summarization, research assistance, risk triage, client-service drafting, coding support, and
analytics. Management emphasizes evaluation before deployment, logging of model behavior, access controls, and escalation
when confidence is low.
• Reusable financial knowledge layer with metadata, source traceability, and quality checks.
• Model evaluation across factuality, groundedness, latency, and cost.
• Human review for material financial, risk, or client-facing decisions.
• Continuous monitoring for data drift, prompt injection, and model performance regression.
07 | 2026 Guidance
full-year 2026 organic net inflows of 2% to 4% of beginning assets and adjusted operating margin of 39% to 41%
08 | Risk Considerations
Fee pressure, client outflows in active strategies, and changes in market valuations can reduce management fees and operating
leverage.
09 | Key Takeaways
• Growth is supported by core franchise momentum and targeted technology investment.
• Management is using automation to improve productivity rather than relying on speculative AI revenue.
• The key monitoring variables are demand, pricing, client retention, credit or market risk, and technology execution.
• The strategic objective is durable earnings quality with disciplined capital allocation.
Forward-looking statements are illustrative and fictional. This presentation is for machine-learning training use only and is not investment advice.

Good morning. This synthetic call is for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026. Statements regarding future performance are
forward-looking and involve risks and uncertainties. All figures discussed are fictional and intended for the FinSight AI training
corpus.
Amelia Grant, Chief Executive Officer
We delivered $1.02 billion of revenue and $0.27 billion of net income. AUM ended at $10.4 trillion, with $118 billion of net new
assets. Private markets and fixed income led flows. Active equity outflows moderated, and institutional retention improved. Our
technology roadmap is focused on research productivity, data quality, and controlled use of generative AI with human review for
investment decisions.
Samuel Ortiz, Chief Financial Officer
Average fee rates were stable overall. Higher AUM, private-markets fundraising, and performance fees supported revenue. We
maintained disciplined compensation growth and continued consolidating technology operations. Full-year planning remains
consistent with organic net inflows of 2% to 4% of beginning assets and adjusted operating margin of 39% to 41%.
Analyst Q&A;
Analyst 1: What is the outlook for active equity?
CEO: The strategy is under ongoing review. We saw modest outflows in the quarter, but
retention improved among larger institutional clients and several teams posted better relative
performance.
Analyst 2: How does private markets affect margins?
CFO: Private markets generally carry attractive fee economics but require distribution and
operational investment. We expect mix shift to support margin over time.
Analyst 3: Where is generative AI being used?
CEO: Research summarization and internal knowledge retrieval are the main pilots. We do not
allow unreviewed generative content to drive client investment decisions.
Closing Remarks
The company reiterated full-year 2026 organic net inflows of 2% to 4% of beginning assets and adjusted operating margin of
39% to 41%, subject to market and execution conditions. Management emphasized disciplined capital allocation, technology
modernization, and risk management.
